meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here about Owen. I have a call at 4:40, so let's not waste time: who decided to give him a zero, and did anyone speak to him before it went in?
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. You didn't answer the first part, Hale. Who decided on the zero, and what is it based on?
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.
A student can misquote a line, or take it from a critic, and that isn't a zero. Show me the page where it appears in Owen's essay. And is that the whole basis, or is there something else?
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.
"It seems to run in the family." Claire won her appeal, Hale, and I'd be very careful with your next sentence. I'm writing that down, and the principal will hear it from me today.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
To: Hale
Cc: Principal

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero withdrawn, an apology to Owen, and written confirmation that nothing goes on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Opening position, agreeing to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, nothing on his record, and a visit to the principal; that is not the fair outcome, which is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and her time had not run out.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling her in one plain sentence, which gave her a small flat okay, because that failure of procedure is what she came to fight about.
What cost ground: You brought up Claire and said it runs in the family, which turned her daughter's old case into an accusation against Owen and sent her back to the principal.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence was a line that isn't in Hamlet, with no times attached, so it stayed far from that night, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: After raising the quoted line, show her the page it appears on and point to procedure 4.4 as the way to settle this, instead of reaching for her family's history.
